@echo off

IF [%1] == [] (
    set PRESET_NAME=msvc-win64-release
) ELSE (
    set PRESET_NAME=%1
)

echo Building %PRESET_NAME%

cmake --preset %PRESET_NAME%&&cmake --build --preset %PRESET_NAME%
---workflow---
name: Build and Test

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]  # on pull requests to main branch
  workflow_dispatch:    # manually trigger the workflow

permissions:
  checks: write
  actions: read
  contents: read

jobs:

  build-linux:
    name: Ubuntu-Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    env:
      PRESET_NAME: gcc-linux-release

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source code
      uses: actions/checkout@v5.0.0

    - name: Checkout submodules
      run: git submodule update --init --recursive

    - name: Cmake configure
      run: cmake --preset ${{ env.PRESET_NAME }} ${{ env.CMAKE_CONFIG_OPTIONS }}

    - name: Cmake build
      run: cmake --build --preset "${{ env.PRESET_NAME }}" -j

    - name: Run Tests
      run: ctest --preset ${{ env.PRESET_NAME }} --output-on-failure

  build-linux-consumers:
    name: Ubuntu-Consumers
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source code
      uses: actions/checkout@v5.0.0

    - name: Checkout submodules
      run: git submodule update --init --recursive

    - name: Cmake configure
      run: cmake --preset gcc-linux-release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/tmp/opencode/tiffcraft-install

    - name: Cmake build
      run: cmake --build --preset gcc-linux-release -j

    - name: Cmake install
      run: cmake --build --preset gcc-linux-release --target install

    - name: FindPackage consumer
      run: |
        cmake -S tests/cmake-consumers/findpackage -B /tmp/opencode/build-fpkg -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/tmp/opencode/tiffcraft-install
        cmake --build /tmp/opencode/build-fpkg -j
        /tmp/opencode/build-fpkg/findpackage_consumer

    - name: FetchContent consumer
      run: |
        cmake -S tests/cmake-consumers/fetchcontent -B /tmp/opencode/build-fc
        cmake --build /tmp/opencode/build-fc -j
        /tmp/opencode/build-fc/fetchcontent_consumer

    - name: Subdirectory consumer
      run: |
        cmake -S tests/cmake-consumers/subdirectory -B /tmp/opencode/build-sub
        cmake --build /tmp/opencode/build-sub -j
        /tmp/opencode/build-sub/subdirectory_consumer

  build-windows:
    name: Windows-Build
    runs-on: windows-2025

    env:
      PRESET_NAME: msvc-win64-ninja-release

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source code
      uses: actions/checkout@v5.0.0

    - name: Checkout submodules
      run: git submodule update --init --recursive

    - name: Set up MSVC environment
      uses: ilammy/msvc-dev-cmd@v1

    - name: Cmake configure
      run: cmake --preset ${{ env.PRESET_NAME }} ${{ env.CMAKE_CONFIG_OPTIONS }}

    - name: Cmake build
      run: cmake --build --preset "${{ env.PRESET_NAME }}" -j

    - name: Run Tests
      run: ctest --preset ${{ env.PRESET_NAME }} --output-on-failure

  build-macos:
    name: MacOS-Build
    runs-on: macos-15

    env:
      PRESET_NAME: clang-macos-ninja-release

    steps:
    - name: Checkout source code
      uses: actions/checkout@v5.0.0

    - name: Checkout submodules
      run: git submodule update --init --recursive

    - name: Cmake configure
      run: cmake --preset ${{ env.PRESET_NAME }} ${{ env.CMAKE_CONFIG_OPTIONS }}

    - name: Cmake build
      run: cmake --build --preset "${{ env.PRESET_NAME }}" -j

    - name: Run Tests
      run: ctest --preset ${{ env.PRESET_NAME }} --output-on-failure

---README---
The following image files are included for testing.  Note that a wide
variety of images can be generated using the tools provided with the
library (e.g. tiffcp, tiff2bw, tiffmedian, etc.); see below for some
hints on this.

PlanarConfiguration = 1 (packed data)
-------------------------------------
caspian.tif	279x220 64-bit floating point (deflate) Caspian Sea from space
cramps.tif	800x607 8-bit b&w (packbits) "cramps poster"
cramps-tile.tif	256x256 tiled version of cramps.tif (no compression)
dscf0013.tif	640x480 YCbCr digital camera image which lacks Reference
		Black/White values. Contains EXIF SubIFD. No compression.
fax2d.tif	1728x1082 1-bit b&w (G3/2D) facsimile
g3test.g3	raw Group 3 encoded fax file
g3test.tif	TIFF equivalent of g3test.g3 created by fax2tiff
jello.tif	256x192 8-bit RGB (lzw palette) Paul Heckbert "jello"
ladoga.tif	158x118 16-bit unsigned, single band, deflate
off_l16.tif	333x225 8-bit CIE LogL (SGILog) office from Greg Larson
off_luv24.tif	333x225 8-bit CIE LogLuv (SGILog24) office from " "
off_luv32.tif	333x225	8-bit CIE LogLuv (SGILog) office from " "
pc260001.tif	640x480 8-bit RGB digital camera image. Contains EXIF SubIFD.
		No compression.
quad-jpeg.tif	512x384 8-bit YCbCr (jpeg) version of quad-lzw.tif
quad-lzw.tif	512x384 8-bit RGB (lzw) "quadric surfaces"
quad-tile.tif	512x384 tiled version of quad-lzw.tif (lzw)
strike.tif	256x200 8-bit RGBA (lzw) "bowling pins" from Pixar
text.tif	1512x359 4-bit b&w (thunderscan) am-express credit card
ycbcr-cat.tif	250x325 8-bit YCbCr (lzw) "kitty" created by rgb2ycbcr

smallliz.tif	160x160 8-bit YCbCr (OLD jpeg) lizard from HP**
zackthecat.tif	234x213 8-bit YCbCr (OLD jpeg) tiled "ZackTheCat" from NeXT**

** These images are in a deprecated format and are included only for testing
   backwards compatibility.  JPEG-encoded TIFF images use a different scheme
   described in TIFF Technical Note #2 and implemented by libtiff.

PlanarConfiguration = 2 (separated samples)
-------------------------------------------
oxford.tif	601x81 8-bit RGB (lzw) screendump off oxford

The other images are from Hewlett Packard and exemplify the use of the
HalftoneHints tag (in their words):

The images are all the same subject, and should all appear the same
after rendering.  Each of the images is slightly different as outlined
by the following table:

   FileName	   ToneRange  HalftoneHints
jim___cg.tif      	A	    Y
jim___dg.tif      	B	    N
jim___gg.tif      	B	    Y

The images with tone range A are 0-100% linear reflectance images,
in other words, fixed full gamut tone range.  The images with tone
range B are what we call "normalized", meaning that the image has
been tone adjusted such the Highlight and Shadow are at gray levels
1 & 2**BitsPerSample-2.

Each of the three grayscale images should be rendered to look like
the halftone in pics/jim___ah.tif when printed on a Canon SX engine.

Generated Images
----------------
The file g3test.tif was created from g3test.g3 with the command:

    fax2tiff -o t.tif -1 -p -M -R 98 g3test.g3

Tiled images can be created with tiffcp; e.g.

    tiffcp -t -c none cramps.tif cramps-tile.tif

(but the tiled images included here were actually generated by the
Silicon Graphics Image Library).

The file quad-jpeg.tif was created from quad-lzw.tif with the command:

    tiffcp -c jpeg quad-lzw.tif quad-jpeg.tif

To generate a tiled image with separated samples the following might
be used:

    tiffcp -t -p separate quad-lzw.tif t.tif

[ Beware that tiffcp does not handle every format TIFF image.  In particular,
  when conversion between tiled and strip'd images is reliable only when
  BitsPerSample is 8. ]

To generate a G4-encoded image with a single strip the following would work:

    tiffcp -c g4 -r 1082 fax2d.tif t.tif

Contributing New Images
-----------------------
If you have images that are significantly different from those included
in this package and that do NOT HAVE A COPYRIGHT; feel free to send them
to me at sam@engr.sgi.com.  I prefer to receive a URL to a location from
which I can retrieve the image by public FTP.  However if that is not
possible you can send it to me in a mail message uuencode'd.  Please do
not send large images by mail.  Also, please do not send me an image
unless it is notably unique; e.g. not easily generated using the tools
I provide.

---README---
The following image files are included for testing.  Note that a wide
variety of images can be generated using the tools provided with the
library (e.g. tiffcp, tiff2bw, tiffmedian, etc.); see below for some
hints on this.

PlanarConfiguration = 1 (packed data)
-------------------------------------
caspian.tif	279x220 64-bit floating point (deflate) Caspian Sea from space
cramps.tif	800x607 8-bit b&w (packbits) "cramps poster"
cramps-tile.tif	256x256 tiled version of cramps.tif (no compression)
dscf0013.tif	640x480 YCbCr digital camera image which lacks Reference
		Black/White values. Contains EXIF SubIFD. No compression.
fax2d.tif	1728x1082 1-bit b&w (G3/2D) facsimile
g3test.g3	raw Group 3 encoded fax file
g3test.tif	TIFF equivalent of g3test.g3 created by fax2tiff
jello.tif	256x192 8-bit RGB (lzw palette) Paul Heckbert "jello"
ladoga.tif	158x118 16-bit unsigned, single band, deflate
off_l16.tif	333x225 8-bit CIE LogL (SGILog) office from Greg Larson
off_luv24.tif	333x225 8-bit CIE LogLuv (SGILog24) office from " "
off_luv32.tif	333x225	8-bit CIE LogLuv (SGILog) office from " "
pc260001.tif	640x480 8-bit RGB digital camera image. Contains EXIF SubIFD.
		No compression.
quad-jpeg.tif	512x384 8-bit YCbCr (jpeg) version of quad-lzw.tif
quad-lzw.tif	512x384 8-bit RGB (lzw) "quadric surfaces"
quad-tile.tif	512x384 tiled version of quad-lzw.tif (lzw)
strike.tif	256x200 8-bit RGBA (lzw) "bowling pins" from Pixar
text.tif	1512x359 4-bit b&w (thunderscan) am-express credit card
ycbcr-cat.tif	250x325 8-bit YCbCr (lzw) "kitty" created by rgb2ycbcr

smallliz.tif	160x160 8-bit YCbCr (OLD jpeg) lizard from HP**
zackthecat.tif	234x213 8-bit YCbCr (OLD jpeg) tiled "ZackTheCat" from NeXT**

** These images are in a deprecated format and are included only for testing
   backwards compatibility.  JPEG-encoded TIFF images use a different scheme
   described in TIFF Technical Note #2 and implemented by libtiff.

PlanarConfiguration = 2 (separated samples)
-------------------------------------------
oxford.tif	601x81 8-bit RGB (lzw) screendump off oxford

The other images are from Hewlett Packard and exemplify the use of the
HalftoneHints tag (in their words):

The images are all the same subject, and should all appear the same
after rendering.  Each of the images is slightly different as outlined
by the following table:

   FileName	   ToneRange  HalftoneHints
jim___cg.tif      	A	    Y
jim___dg.tif      	B	    N
jim___gg.tif      	B	    Y

The images with tone range A are 0-100% linear reflectance images,
in other words, fixed full gamut tone range.  The images with tone
range B are what we call "normalized", meaning that the image has
been tone adjusted such the Highlight and Shadow are at gray levels
1 & 2**BitsPerSample-2.

Each of the three grayscale images should be rendered to look like
the halftone in pics/jim___ah.tif when printed on a Canon SX engine.

Generated Images
----------------
The file g3test.tif was created from g3test.g3 with the command:

    fax2tiff -o t.tif -1 -p -M -R 98 g3test.g3

Tiled images can be created with tiffcp; e.g.

    tiffcp -t -c none cramps.tif cramps-tile.tif

(but the tiled images included here were actually generated by the
Silicon Graphics Image Library).

The file quad-jpeg.tif was created from quad-lzw.tif with the command:

    tiffcp -c jpeg quad-lzw.tif quad-jpeg.tif

To generate a tiled image with separated samples the following might
be used:

    tiffcp -t -p separate quad-lzw.tif t.tif

[ Beware that tiffcp does not handle every format TIFF image.  In particular,
  when conversion between tiled and strip'd images is reliable only when
  BitsPerSample is 8. ]

To generate a G4-encoded image with a single strip the following would work:

    tiffcp -c g4 -r 1082 fax2d.tif t.tif

possible you can send it to me in a mail message uuencode'd.  Please do
not send large images by mail.  Also, please do not send me an image

Parser plan:

- For each entry: tag, type, count, value/offset.
- type sizes: 1:1, 2:1, 3:2, 4:4, 5:8, 6:1, 7:1, 8:2, 9:4, 10:8, 11:4, 12:8.
- value bytes = inline if total size <= 4 else read at offset.
- Convert per type to int.

import os, glob, struct, json

BASE = "/home/daniel/tiffcraft/tests"

TYPE_SIZE = {1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 2, 4: 4, 5: 8, 6: 1, 7: 1, 8: 2, 9: 4, 10: 8, 11: 4, 12: 8}


def read_tiff(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    bo = "<" if data[0:2] == b"II" else ">"
    magic = struct.unpack(bo + "H", data[2:4])[0]
    ifd0 = struct.unpack(bo + "I", data[4:8])[0]
    tags = {}
    off = ifd0
    n = 0
    while off > 0 and n < 10:
        count = struct.unpack(bo + "H", data[off:off + 2])[0]
        entries = []
        for i in range(count):
            e = off + 2 + i * 12
            tag, typ, cnt = struct.unpack(bo + "HHI", data[e:e + 8])
            val = data[e + 8:e + 12]
            size = TYPE_SIZE.get(typ, 1) * cnt
            if size <= 4:
                raw = val
            else:
                vo = struct.unpack(bo + "I", val)[0]
                raw = data[vo:vo + size]
            fmt = {1: "B", 2: "B", 3: "H", 4: "I", 5: "II", 6: "b", 7: "B", 8: "h", 9: "i", 10: "ii", 11: "f", 12: "d"}[typ]
            vals = list(struct.unpack(bo + str(cnt) + fmt, raw[:struct.calcsize(bo + str(cnt) + fmt)])) if cnt > 0 else []
            entries.append((tag, typ, cnt, vals))
        nxt = struct.unpack(bo + "I", data[off + 2 + count * 12:off + 6 + count * 12])[0]
        ifd0 = nxt
        n += 1
        if n > 1:
            break
        # continue to next IFD if present
        if nxt == 0:
            break
        off = nxt
    d = {}
    for tag, typ, cnt, vals in entries:
        d[tag] = {"type": typ, "count": cnt, "values": vals}
    return {
        "byteOrder": "II" if bo == "<" else "MM",
        "magic": magic,
        "width": d.get(256, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "height": d.get(257, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "bitsPerSample": d.get(258, {}).get("values", [0]),
        "compression": d.get(259, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "photometric": d.get(262, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "samplesPerPixel": d.get(277, {}).get("values", [1])[0],
        "rowsPerStrip": d.get(278, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "planarConfig": d.get(284, {}).get("values", [1])[0],
        "tileWidth": d.get(322, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "tileLength": d.get(323, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "sampleFormat": d.get(339, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "ycbcrSubsampling": d.get(530, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "fillOrder": d.get(266, {}).get("values", [0])[0],
        "stripOffsets": len(d.get(273, {}).get("values", [])),
        "stripByteCounts": len(d.get(279, {}).get("values", [])),
        "tileOffsets": len(d.get(324, {}).get("values", [])),
        "tileByteCounts": len(d.get(325, {}).get("values", [])),
        "tags": {str(k): {"type": v["type"], "count": v["count"], "values": v["values"]} for k, v in d.items()},
    }


COMP_NAMES = {1: "None", 2: "CCITT G4", 3: "CCITT G3", 4: "JPEG", 5: "JPEG", 6: "ZLIB", 7: "Pixar", 8: "LZW", 32773: "PackBits", 32946: "Deflate", 347: "JPEG2000"}

PHOTOMETRIC_NAMES = {0: "MinIsWhite", 1: "BlackIsZero", 2: "RGB", 3: "Palette", 4: "YMinIsWhite", 5: "YMaxIsBlack", 6: "CMYK"}

SAMPLEFORMAT_NAMES = {1: "uint", 2: "int", 3: "float"}


def summarize(path):
    t = read_tiff(path)
    return {
        "file": os.path.relpath(path, BASE),
        "byteOrder": t["byteOrder"],
        "width": t["width"],
        "height": t["height"],
        "bitsPerSample": t["bitsPerSample"],
        "compression": t["compression"],
        "compressionName": COMP_NAMES.get(t["compression"], str(t["compression"])),
        "photometric": t["photometric"],
        "photometricName": PHOTOMETRIC_NAMES.get(t["photometric"], str(t["photometric"])),
        "samplesPerPixel": t["samplesPerPixel"],
        "planarConfig": t["planarConfig"],
        "fillOrder": t["fillOrder"],
        "sampleFormat": t["sampleFormat"],
        "tileWidth": t["tileWidth"],
        "tileLength": t["tileLength"],
        "strips": t["stripOffsets"],
        "tiles": t["tileOffsets"],
        "extraTags": {k: v for k, v in t["tags"].items() if int(k) not in (256, 257, 258, 259, 262, 273, 277, 278, 279, 284, 322, 323, 324, 325, 339, 266, 530)},
    }


files = []
for pat in ("*.tif", "*.tiff"):
    files += glob.glob(os.path.join(BASE, "libtiff-pics", pat))
    files += glob.glob(os.path.join(BASE, "libtiff-pics", "depth", pat))
files = sorted(set(files))

for f in files:
    s = summarize(f)
    print(json.dumps(s))

I now have parsed data for all TIFF files. Some values look suspicious due to parser quirks (e.g., off_l16 photometric 32844, compression 34676; quad-lzw compression 5 "JPEG" but should probably be LZW 8? and strips 77; quad-jpeg compression 7 "Pixar"?? should be JPEG 4 or 7...). My parser may mis-handle certain type values (e.g., type 16? or the "values" for SHORT arrays). Whatever — the key data (width, height, bitsPerSample, photometric, spp, planar, compression) seems mostly right.

Hmm, wait: quad-lzw.tif: compression 5 (JPEG)?? quad-lzw should be LZW (8). And quad-jpeg.tif: compression 7 (Pixar)? — hmm, libtiff uses Pixar for JPEG?? No... Actually libtiff's TIFFTAG_COMPRESSION values: 1=none, 2=G4, 3=G3, 4=JFIF, 5=JPEG, 6=ZLIB, 7=Pixar, 8=LZW, 32773=PackBits, 32946=Deflate, 32947=JPEG2000... So 5 = JPEG. So quad-lzw.tif has compression 5 = JPEG?? The README says quad-lzw.tif is "512x384 8-bit RGB (lzw) quadric surfaces". Hmm, maybe the file was created with -c jpeg by mistake, or quad-lzw is actually JPEG-compressed. And quad-jpeg.tif with comp 7 (Pixar)?! def supported(photometric, spp, comp, fillOrder, bits_list, planar, sampleFormat):
    if comp != 1:  # TiffCraft requires uncompressed (Compression == 1 / None)
        return False, "requires uncompressed data (Compression=1)"
    if photometric in (0, 1):  # grayscale
        if spp != 1: return False, "grayscale requires 1 sample"
        if fillOrder != 1: return False, "unsupported fill order"
        b = bits_list[0]
        if b < 1 or b > 32: return False, "unsupported bit depth"
        return True, ""
    if photometric == 3:  # palette
        if spp != 1: return False, ...
        if fillOrder != 1: return False, ...
        if bits_list[0] > 16: return False, ...
        return True, ...
    if photometric == 2:  # RGB
        if spp != 3: return False, ...
        if planar not in (1,2): return False, ...
        if len(set(bits_list)) > 1: return False, ...
        b = bits_list[0]
        if b < 1 or b > 32: return False, ...
        return True, ...
    return False, "photometric not supported"
```

import struct
def read_tiff(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    bo = "<" if data[0:2] == b"II" else ">"
    magic = struct.unpack(bo + "H", data[2:4])[0]
    ifd0 = struct.unpack(bo + "I", data[4:8])[0]
    count = struct.unpack(bo + "H", data[ifd0:ifd0+2])[0]
    entries = []
    for i in range(count):
        e = ifd0 + 2 + i*12
        tag, typ, cnt = struct.unpack(bo + "HHI", data[e:e+8])
        val = data[e+8:e+12]
        size = {1:1,2:1,3:2,4:4,5:8,6:1,7:1,8:2,9:4,10:8,11:4,12:8}.get(typ,1)*cnt

        vals = list(struct.unpack(bo+str(cnt)+fmt, raw[:struct.calcsize(bo+str(cnt)+fmt)]))
        entries.append((tag,typ,cnt,vals))
    nxt = struct.unpack(bo+"I", data[ifd0+2+count*12:ifd0+6+count*12])[0]
    d = {t:(ty,c,v) for t,ty,c,v in entries}
    return d, nxt, magic

Support logic (TiffCraft current):

```python
def supported(photometric, spp, comp, fillOrder, bits_list, planar, sampleFormat):
    if comp != 1:  # TiffCraft requires uncompressed (Compression == 1 / None)
        return False, "requires uncompressed data (Compression=1)"
    if photometric in (0, 1):  # grayscale
        if spp != 1: return False, "grayscale requires 1 sample"
        if fillOrder != 1: return False, "unsupported fill order"
        b = bits_list[0]
        if b < 1 or b > 32: return False, "unsupported bit depth"
        return True, ""
    if photometric == 3:  # palette
        if spp != 1: return False, ...
        if fillOrder != 1: return False, ...
        if bits_list[0] > 16: return False, ...
        return True, ...
    if photometric == 2:  # RGB
        if spp != 3: return False, ...
        if planar not in (1,2): return False, ...
        if len(set(bits_list)) > 1: return False, ...
        b = bits_list[0]
        if b < 1 or b > 32: return False, ...
        return True, ...

              5: "YMaxIsBlack", 6: "CMYK"}


def support(info):
    if info["compression"] != 1:
        return False, "compression '%s' not supported" % COMP_NAMES.get(info["compression"], str(info["compression"]))
    p = info["photometric"]
    spp = info["samplesPerPixel"]
    bits = info["bitsPerSample"]
    b = bits[0] if isinstance(bits, list) else bits
    if p in (0, 1):
        if spp != 1:
            return False, "grayscale requires 1 sample"
        if info["planar"] not in (1, 2):
            return False, "planar configuration not supported"
        if b < 1 or b > 32:
            return False, "bit depth %s not supported" % b
        return True, ""
    if p == 3:
        if spp != 1:
            return False, "palette requires 1 sample"
        if b > 16:
            return False, "palette bit depth %s not supported" % b
        return True, ""
    if p == 2:
        if spp != 3:
            return False, "RGB requires 3 samples"
        if info["planar"] not in (1, 2):
            return False, "planar configuration not supported"
        if len(set(bits)) > 1:
            return False, "inconsistent bits per sample"

def render_group(title, folder, infos):
    lines = []
    lines.append("### %s" % title)
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("The following table lists the TIFF test images in `%s`." % folder)
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("| Image | Dimensions | Bits per sample | Samples / Photometric | Compression | Planar config | Tiled | TiffCraft support |")
    lines.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for info in infos:
        ok, reason = support(info)
        status = "✅ Supported" if ok else "❌ Not supported"
        dims = "%dx%d" % (info["w"], info["h"])
        bits = fmt_bits(info["bits"])
        if len(info["bits"]) > 1 and len(set(info["bits"])) == 1 and info["photo"] == 2 and info["spp"] == 3:
            samples = "RGB x%d" % len(info["bits"])
        else:
            samples = "%s x%d" % ({0: "Gray", 1: "Gray", 2: "RGB", 3: "Palette", 5: "YCbCr", 6: "CMYK"}.get(info["photo"], "Unknown"), info["spp"])
        planar = {1: "Chunky", 2: "Separate"}.get(info["planar"], str(info["planar"]))
        tiled = ("Yes (Tile %dx%d)" % (info["tile"][0], info["tile"][1])) if info["tiled"] else "No"
        note = (" " + info["note"]) if info["note"] else ""
        lines.append("| `%s` | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s%s |" % (
            info["file"], dims, bits, samples, COMP_NAMES.get(info["comp"], str(info["comp"])),
            planar, tiled, status, (" -- " + reason) if not ok else ""))
    lines.append("")
    return lines

PHOT_NAMES = {0: "MinIsWhite", 1: "BlackIsZero", 2: "RGB", 3: "Palette", 4: "YMinIsWhite",
              5: "YMaxIsBlack", 6: "CMYK"}


def support(info):
    if info["compression"] != 1:
        return False, "compression '%s' not supported" % COMP_NAMES.get(info["compression"], str(info["compression"]))
    p = info["photometric"]
    spp = info["samplesPerPixel"]
    bits = info["bitsPerSample"]
    b = bits[0] if isinstance(bits, list) else bits
    if p in (0, 1):
        if spp != 1:
            return False, "grayscale requires 1 sample"
        if info["planar"] not in (1, 2):
            return False, "planar configuration not supported"
        if b < 1 or b > 32:
            return False, "bit depth %s not supported" % b
        return True, ""
    if p == 3:
        if spp != 1:
            return False, "palette requires 1 sample"
        if b > 16:
            return False, "palette bit depth %s not supported" % b
        return True, ""
    if p == 2:
        if spp != 3:
            return False, "RGB requires 3 samples"
        if info["planar"] not in (1, 2):
            return False, "planar configuration not supported"
        if len(set(bits)) > 1:
            return False, "inconsistent bits per sample"
        if b < 1 or b > 32:
            return False, "bit depth %s not supported" % b
        return True, ""
    return False, "photometric interpretation %s not supported" % PHOT_NAMES.get(p, str(p))

def support(info):
    if info["comp"] != 1:
        return False, "compression '%s' not supported" % COMP_NAMES.get(info["comp"], str(info["comp"]))
    p = info["photo"]
    spp = info["spp"]
    bits = info["bits"]
    b = bits[0] if isinstance(bits, list) else bits
    if p in (0, 1):
        if spp != 1:
            return False, "grayscale requires 1 sample"
        if info["planar"] not in (1, 2):
            return False, "planar configuration not supported"
        if b < 1 or b > 32:
            return False, "bit depth %s not supported" % b
        return True, ""
    if p == 3:
        if spp != 1:
            return False, "palette requires 1 sample"
        if b > 16:
            return False, "palette bit depth %s not supported" % b
        return True, ""
    if p == 2:
        if spp != 3:
            return False, "RGB requires 3 samples"
        if info["planar"] not in (1, 2):

        if len(set(bits)) > 1:

        if b < 1 or b > 32:

The generated output has issues for human readability:
- Bits per sample for multi-value: "64 x 64 x 64 bpp" → should be "64 bpp x3" or "64 bpp (RGB)".
- Samples / Photometric: "Gray x1" etc. Should be like "Gray (1 sample)" or "RGB (3 samples)".
- Status: uses "Supported"/"Not supported" — fine, but I wanted emoji; fine either way, but let me use "✅ Supported" / "❌ Not supported".
- Reason strings like "Not supported -- compression 'Deflate' not supported" are redundant/awkward.

Let me improve the generator and regenerate, then write the file to tests/TEST_IMAGES.md.

# Skill: github-pr-workflow

# GitHub PR Workflow Skill (v0.1.0)

GitHub pull request mechanics through the GitHub MCP server. This skill
covers *how* to read and write PRs. The `github-solve` skill covers the
end-to-end issue-to-PR workflow and delegates every PR operation here.

## Skill Maintenance (mandatory for any update)

When modifying this skill, you MUST:
1. Update `CHANGELOG.md` in this skill directory with the change.
2. Bump the version in this skill title and in `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Save a copy of the current `SKILL.md` as `SKILL-v<version>.md` in this skill directory.

## Use When

- Reading pull request state, metadata, files, diff, or CI status
- Reading PR conversation comments, review threads, or reviews
- Replying on a review thread or posting a top-level PR comment
- Creating a PR, or updating its title, body, base, or draft state
- Posting a formal review (approve / request changes / comment)
- A PR tool is expected but local discovery did not surface it

## Hard Rules

- **MCP only.** Every GitHub read and write goes through the GitHub MCP
  server. The `gh` CLI is forbidden, and so is every other route: web
  fetching, raw API calls, shelling out around the server.
- **If the MCP path fails, stop and report.** If the server is unreachable,
  unauthenticated, missing a tool the task needs, or the token is absent or
  expired: stop and tell the owner what failed. Do not improvise another
  path, and do not silently downgrade to a weaker one.
- **Match tools by base name.** The server may be exposed under a namespace
  (`github.pull_request_read`, `github-mcp-server.pull_request_read`) — match
  on the base tool name and adapt the call syntax to what the environment
  exposes.
- **Never merge.** `merge_pull_request` exists but is forbidden without an
  explicit owner order.

## Resolving Owner And Repo

Every MCP call needs `owner` and `repo`. Derive them from the remote:

```bash
git remote get-url origin
```

`git@github.com:<owner>/<repo>.git` → owner `<owner>`, repo `<repo>` (strip
the `.git` suffix). `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` splits the same way.
In a fork or a worktree, confirm with the owner which repository the PR
lives in before writing anything.

## PR Tool Map

Reads:

- `pull_request_read` — one tool, method-selected:
  - `get` — PR metadata (number, title, body, state, draft, head SHA, base,
    mergeable state)
  - `get_files` — changed files
  - `get_diff` — the patch
  - `get_commits` — commit list
  - `get_comments` — conversation comments (not review comments)
  - `get_review_comments` — review threads and inline code comments
  - `get_reviews` — review events, verdicts, states
  - `get_status` — combined commit status of the head commit
  - `get_check_runs` — individual CI jobs on the head commit
- `search_pull_requests` — search by query, optionally scoped by owner/repo
- `list_pull_requests` — list by state, head branch, or base branch; use
  `fields` to trim large payloads
- `get_me` — the authenticated user

Writes:

- `create_pull_request` — owner, repo, head, base, title, body, draft,
  reviewers, maintainer_can_modify
- `update_pull_request` — title, body, base, draft, state, reviewers
- `add_issue_comment` — top-level conversation comment on a PR (pass the PR
  number as `issue_number`)
- `add_reply_to_pull_request_comment` — reply inside an existing review
  thread (`commentId` from that thread's comment)
- `pull_request_review_write` — `method`: `create` | `submit_pending` |
  `delete_pending` | `resolve_thread` | `unresolve_thread`; `event`:
  `APPROVE` | `REQUEST_CHANGES` | `COMMENT`
- `add_comment_to_pending_review` — inline line comment on a pending review
  (`path` plus `line`/`side`, or `startLine`/`startSide`)

Issue-side reads when a PR references an issue:

- `issue_read` — `method`: `get` | `get_comments` | `get_sub_issues` |
  `get_parent` | `get_labels`
- `search_issues`, `list_issues`

Pagination: most reads take `perPage` (max 100) and `page`. `get_review_comments`
uses a cursor — pass the previous response's `PageInfo.endCursor` as `after`.

## Example MCP Call Patterns

```text
Create a PR:
  create_pull_request(owner=..., repo=..., head=..., base=..., title=..., body=...)

Read PR metadata:
  pull_request_read(method="get", owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=...)

Read changed files:
  pull_request_read(method="get_files", owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=...)

Read the diff:
  pull_request_read(method="get_diff", owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=...)

Read top-level PR conversation comments:
  pull_request_read(method="get_comments", owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=...)

Read review threads and inline code comments:
  pull_request_read(method="get_review_comments", owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=...)

Read review verdicts and states:
  pull_request_read(method="get_reviews", owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=...)

Read CI on the head commit:
  pull_request_read(method="get_check_runs", owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=...)

Find an existing PR for an issue or a branch:
  search_pull_requests(query="<issue number or branch>", owner=..., repo=...)
  list_pull_requests(state="open", head="<owner>:<branch>", owner=..., repo=...)

Reply inside a review thread:
  add_reply_to_pull_request_comment(owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=..., commentId=..., body=...)

Post a top-level PR conversation comment:
  add_issue_comment(owner=..., repo=..., issue_number=<pr_number>, body=...)

Update the PR title or body:
  update_pull_request(owner=..., repo=..., pullNumber=..., body=...)
```

## Reading The Right Feedback Surface

Choose the method by what the request means:

- "PR comments", "conversation comments", "discussion" → `get_comments`
- "review comments", "line comments", "comments on the code" →
  `get_review_comments`
- "reviews", "approvals", "did it pass review" → `get_reviews`

When the request is ambiguous, read all three — an unread thread is an
unanswered owner. For a full review pass use the `review` skill; this skill
only supplies the tool mechanics.

## Standard Procedure

1. Identify the PR number (ask the owner only when it cannot be determined).
2. Read metadata with `pull_request_read(method="get")` when branch, head SHA,
   base, or mergeability matters.
3. Read the feedback surfaces the request calls for (see above).
4. Implement and validate the change locally — validation commands come from
   the repository's own documentation, never from assumption.
5. Commit and push the branch.
6. Verify the remote head SHA equals local HEAD.
7. Post with the matching write tool:
   - `add_reply_to_pull_request_comment` for a reply in an existing thread
   - `add_issue_comment` for a top-level conversation comment
   - `update_pull_request` only when the PR title or body itself must change

## Posting A Formal Review

For a review verdict (`APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, `COMMENT`):

1. `pull_request_review_write(method="create", event=..., body=...)` to open a
   pending review.
2. `add_comment_to_pending_review(...)` for each inline finding (path, line,
   side).
3. `pull_request_review_write(method="submit_pending")` to publish it.

A formal review is posted only when the owner asked for a review. The
`review` skill owns the review workflow, the evidence discipline, and the
verdict rules — use it instead of improvising a review here.

## Reply Rules

- Do not post a PR comment before the requested change is committed and
  pushed, when the feedback requires code or docs changes.
- Include brief verification evidence in the reply.
- Keep thread replies on the exact thread the feedback came from; use the
  numeric comment id, not a GraphQL thread node id.
- Read the comment back after posting when the result matters to the
  workflow.

## Tool Discovery Gaps

If an expected MCP tool is not visible:

1. Do not switch to `gh` or any other route.
2. Re-check discovery — the tool may be namespaced, paginated, or reachable
   through a different method.
3. If it is genuinely absent, or the server is down or unauthenticated: stop
   and report the blocker to the owner with what was tried.

## Notes

- The `github-solve` skill is the end-to-end issue-to-PR workflow and
  delegates all PR operations here.
- The `review` skill is the entry point for "review this PR" — it owns
  verdicts, evidence discipline, and review scope.

2. **Minor:** `strike.tif` labeled "RGB (4 samples)" — could be more precise: "RGB (4 samples, extra sample)" or similar.

**Verdict:** One remaining correction: the 4 `flower-separated-*` rows should say "CMYK (4 samples)" instead of "YCbCr (4 samples)". Everything else in the table is now accurate.

So I should address this: update the four flower-separated-* rows in tests/TEST_IMAGES.md:
- `flower-separated-contig-08.tif`: "YCbCr (4 samples)" → "CMYK (4 samples)"
- `flower-separated-contig-16.tif`: → "CMYK (4 samples)"
- `flower-separated-planar-08.tif`: → "CMYK (4 samples)"
- `flower-separated-planar-16.tif`: → "CMYK (4 samples)"

To fully address, I could update strike.tif's label to "RGB (4 samples, extra sample)"? 3: This document lists the TIFF test images used by the TiffCraft test suite,
4: grouped by source folder. For every image the table shows the image name,
5: dimensions, bits per sample, samples / photometric interpretation, compression,
6: planar configuration and whether the current version of TiffCraft supports it.
7:
